html:
SMTO-LLM-0011 — Model stream exceeded a transport safety limit

GUID: bcba78c4-ed81-48d1-b37c-0409045b2400
Slug: llm-stream-event-size-limit
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • One piece of the model's reply was bigger than SMTO accepts at once (about 1 MB), so SMTO stopped the reply. Nothing from it was carried out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to continue in a new message, and ask for the work in smaller parts, for example one file or one section at a time. Say which steps are already done. A reply that writes a very large block at once is more likely to arrive as one oversized piece.
  2. If it happens again even with small requests, select Copy error details and ask the person who manages the model server whether it, or a proxy in front of it, joins replies into very large pieces. Model servers normally send replies in small pieces, and this size limit can't be changed in SMTO's settings.
  3. After they fix the server, on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). SMTO did not act on the oversized reply, so trying the step again is safe once the server sends smaller pieces, and earlier finished steps are kept.

What success looks like

  • The model's reply finishes and the task moves on without this error.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages the model server, with the model and Endpoint you use. Don't try to get around the limit by turning off SMTO's safety checks; it protects SMTO from running out of memory.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A single SSE line or assembled data event from the provider exceeded the decoder's fixed 1 MiB per-event limit, so the stream was rejected (llm_stream_event_size_limit).

What this means

  • A line or assembled event exceeded the decoder’s 1 MiB event bound. The check limits transport memory use, including ignored fields. It is distinct from the model’s context or output-token allowance.

Why this can happen

  • A single stream line or accumulated data event exceeded MAX_EVENT_BYTES.

How to diagnose it

  • Ask the provider operator to inspect event byte sizes and framing. A missing event separator can accumulate data into one event even when individual fragments are small.

How to fix it

  • Check whether the provider or an intermediate proxy coalesces deltas into oversized events (for example a whole tool-call argument in one chunk); MAX_EVENT_BYTES in src/agent_runtime/llm/sse.py is fixed at 1 MiB and counts ignored fields too. Fix the stream framing at the provider or proxy, or request smaller outputs, then resume; this limit is separate from the context window and output-token settings.
  • Ask the provider operator to check the stream format and byte limits with a small test request. Preserve prior tool receipts; do not replay completed operations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Every event in the controlled stream stays within the 1 MiB bound.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The bounded stream decoder rejects the current response; it does not rewrite earlier tool receipts.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
